summary: The appellant, convicted under Sections 302 and 120B IPC and Section 27(1) of the Arms Act, filed an appeal admitted by the Patna High Court in 2009. The appeal was later dismissed in 2015 on the ground that the appellant was absconding. The Supreme Court held that once an appeal is admitted, it must be decided on merits and cannot be dismissed merely due to the appellant's absence or absconding, per settled law in Bani Singh v. State of U.P. Reliance on Shyam Deo Pandey and other cases was noted, but the High Court's deviation from binding precedent was incorrect. The impugned judgment was set aside, and the appeal was remanded for fresh hearing on merits with directions for expeditious disposal.
legal_provisions_cited: Bani Singh & Ors. v. State of U.P.
Shyam Deo Pandey & Ors. v. State of Bihar
Ram Naresh Yadav v. State of Bihar
final_judgment: Impugned judgment set aside; appeal remanded to Patna High Court for fresh hearing on merits; High Court directed to dispose of the appeal expeditiously, preferably within six months; appellant granted liberty to apply for suspension of sentence if not heard within that period.
